On Fri, Nov 19, 2021 at 5:26 PM Lisa Poggiali <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi Matt and others,
I took a stab at trying to make the question more concrete -- it seemed to be getting so abstract it was hard to see
how someone would start answering it - and also capture Diana and Josh's points.
I think the addition of resilience captures that we're interested in both mis/mal/disinformation and the information
ecosystem at large. I added the specific factors and dynamics to signal what existing research has shown us about
the influences on information ecosystems. Would suggest Diana and Josh review since they are up on the existing
literature.
Thanks to Matt for corralling all of us thus far!
best,
Lisa
On Fri, Nov 19, 2021 at 5:25 PM Matthew Baker <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks for all the comments and reflections. I did a quick look but wanted to flag that at this point we should ideally
focus on the first - prioritized - learning question. The remaining questions are here for reference and of course we
can improve upon.
I am going to take note of these points too as we transition to thinking of scoping research as these points should
be considered when we scope and researchers eventually craft a concept.
Many thanks.
Best,
Matt
On Fri, Nov 19, 2021 at 2:28 PM Diana Parzik <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Matt-
Thanks for pulling this together, I think we're on the home stretch. The GEC's program is the Digital Disinfo
Index (DDI) and I'm happy to pull folks together so we can integrate that work into this research.
I added a few comments below Josh's in the questions, mostly minor tweaks (e.g. including mal-information
where we just reference mis- and dis) and also language on 'building resilience'. In the IIR R&D meeting this
morning, Mary Beth and Brian intentionally flagged the NSM LOE on "building resilience' and the research gap
we have in that space. I think this is mostly covered by question 3.
Also, I put some comments in about further clarification for question 5 on 'non-democratic actors'.
Thanks,
Diana
